hero.headline: Indian River County flood watch canceled; flooded roads and schools remain closed
hero.teaser: The National Weather Service canceled Indian River County’s flood watch Friday morning, but flooding and roadway damage continued to disrupt travel. County schools remained closed Friday.
hero.body:
The National Weather Service canceled the flood watch for Indian River County Friday morning, but flooding and roadway damage continued to disrupt travel, including in Vero Lake Estates. The School District of Indian River County remained closed Friday. Additional showers remain possible, though the heaviest rainfall threat is farther north, according to Indian River County Emergency Services.

 In Vero Lake Estates, 104th Avenue between 87th and 93rd streets and 83rd Street between 91st and 93rd avenues are closed. Elsewhere, 130th Street is closed, along with 79th Street west of 130th Avenue because of a roadway washout. Roadway damage also closed 13th Street SW east of 66th Avenue SW.

 Partial blockages were reported on U.S. 1 near Barber Street, at 82nd Avenue near the entrance to Heritage Plantation, and on Skyline Drive from Periwinkle to Barber Street. Old Dixie Highway SW had flooding and partial blockages at several locations. Drivers can check the county’s live road closure map for additional closures and updates.

 Officials urged drivers to check conditions before traveling, allow extra time for detours and never drive through flooded roads. Water needs time to recede, and damaged roads must be assessed and repaired before they can safely reopen. Crews are working in affected areas, and drivers are asked to give them room and follow barricades.

 Marian Fell Library and the Veterans Services office in Sebastian remain closed. The Indian River County Shooting Range, Gifford Aquatic Center and North County Aquatic Center are open Friday. Families can check the school district’s website for updates on the district closure.

cards.headline: Martin County cancels Kanner Highway data center meeting, promises public forums
cards.teaser: Martin County canceled a Friday staff meeting about a proposed data center off Kanner Highway, citing overwhelming public interest, and promised future public meetings and workshop
cards.body:
Martin County canceled a Friday staff meeting about a proposed data center off Kanner Highway, citing overwhelming public interest, and promised future public meetings and workshops. Residents gathered outside the Martin County Administrative Center anyway, demanding answers about the development west of Interstate 95, roughly half a mile from Crystal Lake Elementary School. The project remains under review and could qualify for administrative approval without a public hearing or a recorded vote by county commissioners.

 The county announced the cancellation Thursday evening, less than 17 hours before the meeting was scheduled to begin. Deputy Growth Management Director Pete Walden said members of the public had requested the informal question-and-answer session with Growth Management Department staff. He said it was intended for questions, rather than a decision on the application, but information circulating online created the impression that officials were privately considering approval.

 Interest eventually exceeded the county’s capacity to accommodate attendees, he said. “We could not accommodate that. We didn't have any rooms or anything available for that size,” Walden said.

 The potential approval process is another focus of residents’ objections. A county ordinance adopted in 2010 established administrative approval for certain targeted industries to encourage economic development. Data centers fall within those classifications.

 Walden said an existing planned unit development agreement also covers the proposal and allows qualifying targeted industries on platted industrial lots to receive administrative approval. Commissioners approved a one-year moratorium on data centers Oct. 27 while the county reviews its development regulations. County officials said this application was submitted before the moratorium was proposed, making the project exempt from that temporary restriction.

 Residents raised concerns about potential noise from cooling equipment, water consumption, electricity demand, higher utility bills, wildlife displacement, property values and possible health effects on children at Crystal Lake Elementary School. Those concerns are questions about potential impacts, rather than established consequences of the development. Chris McIntyre, whose son graduated from the school, was among those seeking answers Friday. “We need answers, and we need them quick,” he said. Dan Wilson, president of the Locks Landing homeowners association, represents a community less than two miles from the proposed site.

 Walden said the county will review potential impacts before deciding whether to approve the project. A staff report examining the application is expected in December. After that report, county officials plan a public forum where residents can ask questions and learn more about the development, likely including a presentation from the applicant.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie road partially collapses after flooding as neighbor warns of growing hole
cards.teaser: A road and nearby property in Port St. Lucie partially collapsed during historic flooding, leaving a hole that a neighbor says has continued to grow each day. The damage developed
cards.body:
A road and nearby property in Port St. Lucie partially collapsed during historic flooding, leaving a hole that a neighbor says has continued to grow each day. The damage developed as floodwater poured into the area and the ground buckled before giving way. Sections of the road and adjoining property fell into the hole, with aerial views showing the extent of the collapse. Yoshi Duran, who lives nearby, pointed out the damage close to her home and described how much of the area had been underwater. “All this was flooded,” she said.

 Duran said the widening hole has left her worried about another collapse and what the damage could mean for the homes around it. Her concern is not just about the road that has already fallen away, but also about whether more ground could give way as the hole expands. “It’s not anything to laugh about. It is a dangerous situation because they’re not knowing when it can cave in,” Duran said.

 She said the hole has grown daily since the flooding. As she watches the damage spread, she is pressing the city for answers about the situation near her home.

 City public information officer Scott Samples said excess water on the road and in a culvert beneath it caused the damage. Officials are aware of the collapse and are assessing how best to repair it. Samples said the city wants to move quickly, but determining the right approach takes time. “We want to repair these as quickly as we possibly can.

 Unfortunately, it takes some time,” he said. The city is still working out how to address the damaged area, and Samples said studies may be necessary before crews can begin the repair work. Samples said the city’s goal is to make sure the work is done properly, even if that requires further evaluation before construction starts. “You want to make sure you’re doing it as well and as correctly as you possibly can.

 So that may require some studies to take place before you actually start the work,” he said. For Duran, the continuing growth of the hole makes answers urgent. “We understand everybody is short-staffed. But we need answers,” she said.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast traffic report: I-95 ramp closures, roadwork planned Nov. 20–Dec. 4
cards.teaser: I-95 ramps at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway, Port St. Lucie neighborhood streets and 90th Avenue near Sebastian face scheduled closures Nov. 20–Dec. 4.
cards.body:
Drivers across the Treasure Coast face two weeks of construction-related lane and ramp closures around Thanksgiving, including overnight work on Interstate 95 in Martin and St. Lucie counties, detours on neighborhood streets in Port St. Lucie and a planned overnight closure of 90th Avenue near Sebastian.

 The Florida Department of Transportation's traffic report issued Friday, Nov. 20, covers Nov. 20 through Dec. 4 , a longer-than-usual period that spans the Thanksgiving holiday. Many major construction projects will pause Wednesday, Nov. 25, through Sunday, Nov. 29 , although individual work schedules vary.

 The biggest immediate disruptions are planned for Sunday and Monday nights, Nov. 22–23 , at the I-95 interchange with SW Martin Highway. Additional ramp closures near Kanner Highway and overnight restrictions in Sebastian are scheduled after the holiday. Drivers should follow posted detour signs and allow extra travel time.

 Biggest closures to know about

 I-95 at SW Martin Highway, Exit 110, Martin County: The northbound exit ramp to Martin Highway and the northbound entrance ramp from Martin Highway are scheduled for separate closures 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, and Monday, Nov. 23 . Only one ramp will close at a time. FDOT lists Nov. 30–Dec. 3 as contingency nights.

 I-95 at SW Kanner Highway, Exit 101, Martin County: The southbound entrance and exit ramps are each scheduled for overnight closures 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Nov. 30–Dec. 3 , with one ramp closed at a time. Detours will use Bridge Road and Pratt Whitney Road for the entrance closure and a turnaround via Bridge Road for the exit closure.

 Port St. Lucie neighborhood streets: Extended closures for drainage and utility work may affect SW Jaslo, Koler, McCoy, McCullough and McHord avenues and SW Paar Drive starting 7 a.m. Monday, Nov. 23 , with roads scheduled to reopen by 5 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 24 .

 Contingency dates are Nov. 30–Dec. 4. Adjacent roads will not close simultaneously, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

 SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard: Full overnight closures are planned intermittently between SW Fisherman and SW Liberty avenues, 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. Nov. 23–Dec. 4 , excluding the Thanksgiving work pause. Detours will use Fisherman, Liberty and Pisano streets.

 90th Avenue near Sebastian: Portions of S.R. 510/90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street are scheduled for intermittent overnight full closures 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. Nov. 30–Dec. 3 for drainage work. Detours use 85th Street, U.S. 1 and Sebastian Boulevard . FDOT lists Dec. 6–10 as contingency dates.

 I-95 through Martin and St. Lucie counties: Up to two lanes in each direction may close overnight in several work zones. The Thanksgiving construction pause applies to the mainline resurfacing projects described below.

 Martin County

 I-95 ramp closures and resurfacing

 I-95 from SE Bridge Road to the Martin–St. Lucie county line: Up to two southbound lanes will close 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. , and up to two northbound lanes 8:30 p.m. to 6:30 a.m. , beginning Sunday, Nov. 22. FDOT lists the resurfacing schedule through Dec. 24, with no work Nov. 25–29 for Thanksgiving. The report includes the longer schedule so drivers can plan beyond Dec. 4.

 At SW Martin Highway, Exit 110 , the northbound exit closure will require drivers to continue to SW Becker Road, Exit 114 , take westbound Becker Road and use the southbound I-95 entrance ramp to return to the Martin Highway exit. During the separate northbound entrance closure, the detour uses eastbound Martin Highway, northbound SW Newfield Parkway and westbound Becker Road to enter I-95 northbound at Becker Road. Both closures are scheduled for Nov. 22 and 23 from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m.

 At Kanner Highway, Exit 101 , the southbound entrance ramp closure is scheduled Nov. 30–Dec. 3 from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. FDOT directs motorists via Kanner Highway, Pratt Whitney Road and SE Bridge Road to rejoin I-95 southbound. The separate southbound exit ramp closure uses Bridge Road, Exit 96 , with motorists returning north toward Kanner Highway.

 Weather contingency dates for both Kanner closures are Dec. 6–10. Only one ramp will close at a time.

 Hobe Sound, Jensen Beach and Palm City

 U.S. 1 in Hobe Sound, between SE Dixie Highway and SE Osprey Street: One northbound lane may close 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. and 9 p.m. to 7 a.m. Nov. 23–Dec. 4 for road construction. Southbound restrictions are scheduled 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Nov. 23–Dec. 4 and 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Nov. 22–Dec. 3 . Access to homes and businesses will be maintained, and no work is scheduled Nov. 25–29.

 S.R. A1A/NE Ocean Boulevard near the Jensen Beach Causeway: One lane may close intermittently in either direction between NE Shore Village Terrace and the causeway Nov. 23–Dec. 4 for drainage and pavement widening. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic. Additional overnight paving is planned 7:30 p.m. to 6 a.m. Nov. 30–Dec. 4 .

 S.R. 714/SW Martin Highway in Palm City: One lane may close in either direction between SW Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard, 7 p.m. to 6 a.m. Nov. 22–Dec. 3 , for resurfacing, widening and light installation. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic. No work is scheduled Nov. 25–29.

 Stuart and other local work

 FDOT also lists daytime utility restrictions, generally 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Nov. 23–Dec. 4 , on several roads: SW Martin Highway near Martin Downs Boulevard and SW 42nd Avenue in Palm City; SE Monterey Road between U.S. 1 and SE Dixie Highway in Stuart; U.S. 1 near SE Indian Street, SE Monterey Road and NW 16th Street; SW Kanner Highway between SW Gaines Avenue and SW Salerno Road; and NE Ocean Boulevard near Joe's Point Road and Tiger Shores Beach .

 In Port Mayaca, SW Conners Highway near the Port Mayaca Polo Club and the Florida Trail recreation-area trailhead may have intermittent daytime lane closures during the same period. Thanksgiving work breaks are listed for these utility operations.

 St. Lucie County

 I-95 overnight lane closures

 I-95 between SW Gatlin Boulevard and south of SW Becker Road: Two northbound lanes may close 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. and two southbound lanes 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. , Nov. 22–Dec. 4. Lane shifts are possible during resurfacing and pavement-marking work. No work is scheduled Nov. 25–29.

 I-95 between Glades Cut Off Road and south of S.R. 70/Okeechobee Road: Shoulders in both directions may close 6:30 a.m. to 7 p.m. , while up to two lanes may close 8 p.m. to 6:30 a.m. Nov. 22–Dec. 4 , for grading, signs and road improvements. No work is scheduled Nov. 25–29.

 FDOT separately lists intermittent overnight utility lane closures on I-95 between mile markers 125 and 133 , from just north of Midway Road toward Orange Avenue, 8 p.m. to 5 a.m. Nov. 30–Dec. 4 .

 Port St. Lucie Boulevard and neighborhood detours

 The SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project includes extended closures on SW Jaslo Avenue between SW Jacoby Avenue and SW Paar Drive; SW Koler Avenue near SW Kober Road; SW McCoy Avenue near SW Jamros Street; SW McCullough Avenue between SW Jaslo Avenue and the boulevard; SW McHord Avenue near SW Kabane Street; and both directions of SW Paar Drive near the boulevard .

 These closures may begin at 7 a.m. Nov. 23 and are expected to end by 5 p.m. Nov. 24 , with Nov. 30–Dec. 4 reserved as contingency dates. FDOT says adjacent road closures will not occur simultaneously, and access to residences and businesses will remain available. Motorists should follow the posted neighborhood detours.

 A separate series of full nighttime closures on SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between SW Fisherman and SW Liberty avenues is scheduled intermittently 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. Nov. 23–Dec. 4 for utility work, excluding Nov. 25–29. The signed detour for through traffic uses SW Fisherman Avenue, SW Pisano Street and SW Liberty Avenue .

 Other intermittent lane closures are listed on SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between SW Jordin Avenue and SW Alcantarra Boulevard, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Nov. 23–Dec. 4 .

 Port St. Lucie Boulevard, U.S. 1 and Midway Road

 SE Port St. Lucie Boulevard between SE Seafury Lane and SE Lennard Road: One lane may close during the day, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Nov. 23–Dec. 4 , while two lanes may close intermittently overnight, 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Nov. 22–Dec. 4 , for road and striping work.

 U.S. 1 between SE Jennings Road and NW Golden Oak Trail: One lane in either direction may close 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Nov. 23–Dec. 4 and 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Nov. 22–Dec. 4 for inspection and striping work.

 U.S. 1 between Midway Road and south of Edwards Road: One lane may close in either direction 9:30 p.m. to 6:30 a.m. Nov. 22–Dec. 3 for lighting installation, with intermittent daytime shoulder closures Nov. 23–Dec. 4.

 Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road: Intermittent lane restrictions continue during daytime hours, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. weekdays , and overnight, 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday , through December as widening work progresses.

 Fort Pierce and the North Causeway

 The new fixed S.R. A1A North Causeway Bridge is open to motorists, but nearby road construction continues. FDOT lists intermittent lane restrictions along U.S. 1 near Juanita Avenue, Old Dixie Highway between Sunny Lane and Juanita Avenue, Harbortown Drive, and A1A east of the new bridge during daylight work hours through December.

 The old drawbridge is no longer carrying vehicle traffic. The bicycle lanes and north-side shared-use path remain closed while construction continues; pedestrians are directed to the south-side sidewalk.

 FDOT prohibits lane and shoulder closures related to the North Causeway project Nov. 25–29 to reduce Thanksgiving travel impacts.

 Additional daytime utility work may affect U.S. 1, S.R. 70/Okeechobee Road, South Kings Highway, Midway Road and Turnpike Feeder Road in Fort Pierce. Specific blocks and dates vary; many are scheduled between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. through Dec. 4.

 Indian River County

 Oslo Road interchange finished; Sebastian-area restrictions remain

 FDOT reports the new I-95/Oslo Road interchange project was formally accepted Nov. 17 . All lanes are open , marking a change from recent traffic reports that listed overnight interchange ramp closures.

 S.R. 510/90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street: One lane may close intermittently in either direction 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Nov. 22–Dec. 4 for construction, with no work Nov. 25–29. An additional intermittent full road closure is planned 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. Nov. 30–Dec. 3 for drainage work. Northbound traffic will detour using 85th Street, U.S. 1 and Sebastian Boulevard ; southbound traffic uses the same connecting roads in reverse.

 Access to homes and businesses will be maintained. FDOT lists Dec. 6–10 as contingency dates.

 Signal work is also planned at the 90th Avenue and Sebastian Boulevard intersection from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Thursday, Dec. 3 , with intermittent restrictions.

 Sebastian Inlet Bridge work and parking

 S.R. A1A/Jimmy Buffett Memorial Highway at Sebastian Inlet: Traffic is using a temporary shifted roadway alignment established in October. FDOT expects the temporary pattern to remain through late 2028 as the bridge replacement advances.

 One northbound or southbound lane and/or shoulder may close as needed 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 7 a.m. to 1 p.m. Friday , excluding weekends and holidays, through December. Only one lane will close at a time, with flaggers directing motorists. FDOT says the project's lane and shoulder closures are not permitted Nov. 25–29.

 Sections of the north and south Sebastian Inlet State Park parking lots remain partially closed during bridge construction. The park remains open, but parking is limited, the observation decks beneath the bridge are closed and south-jetty access from the south parking lot is closed . Access to the boat ramp will be maintained.

 Vero Beach road and utility work

 Several Vero Beach-area roads may have daytime restrictions, generally 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. : northbound U.S. 1 between Bridge Boulevard and Durrance Road; northbound U.S. 1 between 61st Place and 63rd Street; U.S. 1 between 24th Street and 21st Street; and S.R. A1A near Mango Road and Shoe Drive . These are scheduled on various dates through Dec. 4, with Thanksgiving work pauses on many projects.

 Oslo Road between Old Dixie Highway SW and Timber Ridge Trail SW may have intermittent lane restrictions 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Nov. 30–Dec. 4 for utility work. Additional lane restrictions are listed along S.R. 60 near 97th Road, 98th Avenue, 33rd Avenue and 26th Avenue , and along S.R. A1A near Round Island Place and Ocean Estates Drive .

 Before you travel

 These are planned construction and maintenance restrictions , not reports of traffic incidents or guarantees that every closure will occur. Dates and work hours may change because of weather, contractor schedules or other conditions.

 For real-time interstate traffic, consult Florida 511 . For FDOT District 4 construction notices and updated lane-closure schedules, visit D4FDOT.com . This roundup is based on FDOT's Treasure Coast Traffic Report issued Nov. 20, 2026 , covering Nov. 20–Dec. 4 .

An additional intermittent full road closure is planned 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. Nov. 30–Dec. 3 for drainage work. Northbound traffic will detour using 85th Street, U.S. 1 and Sebastian Boulevard ; southbound traffic uses the same connecting roads in reverse.

 Access to homes and businesses will be maintained. FDOT lists Dec. 6–10 as contingency dates.

 Signal work is also planned at the 90th Avenue and Sebastian Boulevard intersection from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Thursday, Dec. 3 , with intermittent restrictions.

 Sebastian Inlet Bridge work and parking

 S.R. A1A/Jimmy Buffett Memorial Highway at Sebastian Inlet: Traffic is using a temporary shifted roadway alignment established in October. FDOT expects the temporary pattern to remain through late 2028 as the bridge replacement advances.

 One northbound or southbound lane and/or shoulder may close as needed 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 7 a.m. to 1 p.m. Friday , excluding weekends and holidays, through December. Only one lane will close at a time, with flaggers directing motorists. FDOT says the project's lane and shoulder closures are not permitted Nov. 25–29.

 Sections of the north and south Sebastian Inlet State Park parking lots remain partially closed during bridge construction. The park remains open, but parking is limited, the observation decks beneath the bridge are closed and south-jetty access from the south parking lot is closed . Access to the boat ramp will be maintained.

 Vero Beach road and utility work

 Several Vero Beach-area roads may have daytime restrictions, generally 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. : northbound U.S. 1 between Bridge Boulevard and Durrance Road; northbound U.S. 1 between 61st Place and 63rd Street; U.S. 1 between 24th Street and 21st Street; and S.R. A1A near Mango Road and Shoe Drive . These are scheduled on various dates through Dec. 4, with Thanksgiving work pauses on many projects.

 Oslo Road between Old Dixie Highway SW and Timber Ridge Trail SW may have intermittent lane restrictions 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Nov. 30–Dec. 4 for utility work. Additional lane restrictions are listed along S.R. 60 near 97th Road, 98th Avenue, 33rd Avenue and 26th Avenue , and along S.R. A1A near Round Island Place and Ocean Estates Drive .

 Before you travel

 These are planned construction and maintenance restrictions , not reports of traffic incidents or guarantees that every closure will occur. Dates and work hours may change because of weather, contractor schedules or other conditions.

 For real-time interstate traffic, consult Florida 511 . For FDOT District 4 construction notices and updated lane-closure schedules, visit D4FDOT.com . This roundup is based on FDOT's Treasure Coast Traffic Report issued Nov. 20, 2026 , covering Nov. 20–Dec. 4 .

hero.headline: Martin County cancels Kanner Highway data center meeting, promises public forums
hero.teaser: Martin County canceled a Friday staff meeting about a proposed data center off Kanner Highway, citing overwhelming public interest, and promised future public meetings and workshop
hero.body:
Martin County canceled a Friday staff meeting about a proposed data center off Kanner Highway, citing overwhelming public interest, and promised future public meetings and workshops. Residents gathered outside the Martin County Administrative Center anyway, demanding answers about the development west of Interstate 95, roughly half a mile from Crystal Lake Elementary School. The project remains under review and could qualify for administrative approval without a public hearing or a recorded vote by county commissioners.

 The county announced the cancellation Thursday evening, less than 17 hours before the meeting was scheduled to begin. Deputy Growth Management Director Pete Walden said members of the public had requested the informal question-and-answer session with Growth Management Department staff. He said it was intended for questions, rather than a decision on the application, but information circulating online created the impression that officials were privately considering approval.

 Interest eventually exceeded the county’s capacity to accommodate attendees, he said. “We could not accommodate that. We didn't have any rooms or anything available for that size,” Walden said.

 The potential approval process is another focus of residents’ objections. A county ordinance adopted in 2010 established administrative approval for certain targeted industries to encourage economic development. Data centers fall within those classifications.

 Walden said an existing planned unit development agreement also covers the proposal and allows qualifying targeted industries on platted industrial lots to receive administrative approval. Commissioners approved a one-year moratorium on data centers Oct. 27 while the county reviews its development regulations. County officials said this application was submitted before the moratorium was proposed, making the project exempt from that temporary restriction.

 Residents raised concerns about potential noise from cooling equipment, water consumption, electricity demand, higher utility bills, wildlife displacement, property values and possible health effects on children at Crystal Lake Elementary School. Those concerns are questions about potential impacts, rather than established consequences of the development. Chris McIntyre, whose son graduated from the school, was among those seeking answers Friday. “We need answers, and we need them quick,” he said. Dan Wilson, president of the Locks Landing homeowners association, represents a community less than two miles from the proposed site.

 Walden said the county will review potential impacts before deciding whether to approve the project. A staff report examining the application is expected in December. After that report, county officials plan a public forum where residents can ask questions and learn more about the development, likely including a presentation from the applicant.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie road partially collapses after flooding as neighbor warns of growing hole
hero.teaser: A road and nearby property in Port St. Lucie partially collapsed during historic flooding, leaving a hole that a neighbor says has continued to grow each day. The damage developed
hero.body:
A road and nearby property in Port St. Lucie partially collapsed during historic flooding, leaving a hole that a neighbor says has continued to grow each day. The damage developed as floodwater poured into the area and the ground buckled before giving way. Sections of the road and adjoining property fell into the hole, with aerial views showing the extent of the collapse. Yoshi Duran, who lives nearby, pointed out the damage close to her home and described how much of the area had been underwater. “All this was flooded,” she said.

 Duran said the widening hole has left her worried about another collapse and what the damage could mean for the homes around it. Her concern is not just about the road that has already fallen away, but also about whether more ground could give way as the hole expands. “It’s not anything to laugh about. It is a dangerous situation because they’re not knowing when it can cave in,” Duran said.

 She said the hole has grown daily since the flooding. As she watches the damage spread, she is pressing the city for answers about the situation near her home.

 City public information officer Scott Samples said excess water on the road and in a culvert beneath it caused the damage. Officials are aware of the collapse and are assessing how best to repair it. Samples said the city wants to move quickly, but determining the right approach takes time. “We want to repair these as quickly as we possibly can.

 Unfortunately, it takes some time,” he said. The city is still working out how to address the damaged area, and Samples said studies may be necessary before crews can begin the repair work. Samples said the city’s goal is to make sure the work is done properly, even if that requires further evaluation before construction starts. “You want to make sure you’re doing it as well and as correctly as you possibly can.

 So that may require some studies to take place before you actually start the work,” he said. For Duran, the continuing growth of the hole makes answers urgent. “We understand everybody is short-staffed. But we need answers,” she said.

hero.headline: Indian River County flood watch canceled; flooded roads and schools remain closed
hero.teaser: The National Weather Service canceled Indian River County’s flood watch Friday morning, but flooding and roadway damage continued to disrupt travel. County schools remained closed Friday.
hero.body:
The National Weather Service canceled the flood watch for Indian River County Friday morning, but flooding and roadway damage continued to disrupt travel, including in Vero Lake Estates. The School District of Indian River County remained closed Friday. Additional showers remain possible, though the heaviest rainfall threat is farther north, according to Indian River County Emergency Services.

 In Vero Lake Estates, 104th Avenue between 87th and 93rd streets and 83rd Street between 91st and 93rd avenues are closed. Elsewhere, 130th Street is closed, along with 79th Street west of 130th Avenue because of a roadway washout. Roadway damage also closed 13th Street SW east of 66th Avenue SW.

 Partial blockages were reported on U.S. 1 near Barber Street, at 82nd Avenue near the entrance to Heritage Plantation, and on Skyline Drive from Periwinkle to Barber Street. Old Dixie Highway SW had flooding and partial blockages at several locations. Drivers can check the county’s live road closure map for additional closures and updates.

 Officials urged drivers to check conditions before traveling, allow extra time for detours and never drive through flooded roads. Water needs time to recede, and damaged roads must be assessed and repaired before they can safely reopen. Crews are working in affected areas, and drivers are asked to give them room and follow barricades.

 Marian Fell Library and the Veterans Services office in Sebastian remain closed. The Indian River County Shooting Range, Gifford Aquatic Center and North County Aquatic Center are open Friday. Families can check the school district’s website for updates on the district closure.
